decisions.id: B3-9 T140 held for the GM after the named route was attempted
decisions.summary: the seating's admission (tree.admits, which the gap pass asks of each household's way) asked the settle's 7 ft fabric reading in two forms: the manifest's yard lists only, which had no effect; then the seated yards and gardens from geom, after which the reference roll Inashiro refused its web. Earlier, a way-out strip was tried and also refused at the reference. All reverted. The cause found was each farm's own garden. The remaining route is a seating that lays the garden, the fixtures and the way out together (E3, row 748). T140 stays open and the batch is held; the GM is asked for a waiver or a go-ahead at band-3 sign-off
decisions.why: Round 1 required the route the plan itself named to be tried before any waiver: the seating's own search asking each household's way out with its fixtures in place. That route has now been tried at the place named. tree.admits is the predicate the gap pass asks of each way before it admits it (gap_ways, feature 318). It was tried in two forms, measured, and reverted, and that meets XIII's 'genuinely attempted'. The same pattern was ruled LEGITIMATE at W54-7 round 3. What is left is a layout change across the seating's modules. That is XIV's overhaul exception, delivered with the measurement (fourteen first legs, the fabric an owner-less garden), the mechanism (each change moves the exit, and the web's outcome moves chaotically with it) and a sketch. A wrong guess at that change would take hours to unwind. Nothing is narrowed: T140 stays open, the batch stays off main, and band 3 owes the GM's personal sign-off anyway. Deferring the question to the feature's end is what the GM's request asks for ('defer it to the end of the feature'). A waiver is still the GM's to grant and is not presumed.
